literal: The ruin of those who did evil deeds is like [their] shadow staying at [their] feet without leaving.
translation: The ruin of those who commit evil deeds will pursue and destroy them, just as one's own shadow stays at one's feet and never leaves.
modern: தீய செயல்களைச் செய்தவர்கள் அழிவது, அவர்களுடைய நிழல் அவர்களை விட்டு நீங்காமல் அவர்களுடைய காலடியிலேயே தங்கியிருப்பதைப் போன்றது ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet warns that escape from the consequences of evil deeds is impossible. Just as a person's shadow is inseparable from them and stays right at their feet ('அடி', written here as 'அஇ') wherever they go, ruin ('கெடுதல்') will inevitably follow and catch up with those who do evil ('தீயவை செய்தார்'). The metaphor of the shadow ('நிழல்') emphasizes that retribution is not an external force but an inherent, inescapable consequence of one's own actions.
